title.en: Explain why the order of conditions matters
Use indentation correctly and spot IndentationError

say.en: A traffic signal has three colours, and an electricity bill has different rates for different slabs. When there are more than two choices we climb an if..elif ladder. In this lesson: Write an if..elif..else ladder.
Explain why the order of conditions matters.
Use indentation correctly and spot IndentationError.

body.en: When there are several conditions, Python uses elif (short for else if). The conditions are checked from top to bottom; the block of the first condition that is True is executed and the rest of the *ladder* is skipped. The final else is optional and runs only when no condition is True. A ladder can have any number of elif parts.

points.en: First True condition wins; the rest are skipped

title.en: On the board: A grade ladder

say.en: Let us build a grade ladder for marks. Each rung is one condition.
72 is not 90 or more, so we go to the next rung: is it 60 or more?
Yes. So Grade B is printed and the remaining rungs are never checked.
If every condition were False, the else block, Fail, would run.
Indentation shows which statements belong to each block. Four spaces is the usual step.

body.en: Python uses *indentation*, the leading white space at the start of a line, to group statements into a block. All statements of a block must have the same indentation; a new block (after a colon) is indented one more level, usually 4 spaces. Wrong indentation gives an IndentationError or changes the meaning of the program. An if inside another if is called a nested if, and its block is indented further.

say.en: Python uses indentation, the leading white space at the start of a line, to group statements into a block. All statements of a block must have the same indentation; a new block after a colon is indented one more level, usually 4 spaces. Wrong indentation gives an IndentationError or changes the meaning of the program. An if inside another if is called a nested if, and its block is indented further. Same indentation equals same block.

body.en: Every line that ends with a colon (if, elif, else, for, while) must be followed by at least one line indented one level more. When the indentation goes back, the block is over.

mnemonic.en: C-I: Colon → Indent. Dedent → block ends.

narration.en: Remember C-I: a colon is always followed by an indent, and going back to the left ends the block.

problem.en: Print whether num = -4 is positive, negative or zero.

narration.en: Three choices need one if, one elif and one else.

say.en: Three choices need one if, one elif and one else. Print whether num equals minus 4 is positive, negative or zero.
num equals minus 4.
if num is greater than 0.
print("Positive").
elif num is less than 0.
print("Negative").
else.
print("Zero").
So the answer is Negative.
